fichas.title: Hospital useful life and equipment replacement
fichas.summary: Hospital structures, walls, fittings, and finishes have different lifetimes. A framed structure can allow flexible wall and partition layouts. Medical-equipment replacement and the ability to install or remove equipment without disrupting the load-bearing structure should be considered in the design.
uses: Plan for changing medical equipment and spatial arrangements

fichas.title: Hospital site selection and orientation
fichas.summary: Hospital sites should provide room for the building, access, and possible extensions, and should be quiet and free of contaminated ground. Site planning should account for separated access roads for visitors and patients, staff, goods, and emergency vehicles, as well as a helicopter pad. Treatment and operational rooms are best oriented between north-west and north-east; patient-room fronts are favourably oriented south-east or south-west.
uses: Select a suitable site and allow for possible extensions
Separate access for visitors and patients, staff, goods, and emergency vehicles
Orient treatment and operational rooms and patient-room fronts appropriately

fichas.title: Hospital building forms and circulation
fichas.summary: Hospital form is strongly influenced by access and routing. Early planning should determine whether circulation uses a main corridor with branches or radiates from a cruciform core. Extensions and construction phases should be considered. The vertical arrangement should separate care, examination and treatment, supply and waste disposal, patient delivery, service, storage, administration, and clinical medical functions while keeping them quickly accessible. The page illustrates open and enclosed main-corridor arrangements, care areas above or beside examination and treatment areas, and extension possibilities.
uses: Separate hospital functions while maintaining quick access
Allow for extensions and construction phases

fichas.title: Hospital vertical structure and floor heights
fichas.summary: An example vertical structure places a helipad and air-conditioning plant on the top floor; care wards on the second and third floors; operating theatres, central sterilisation, intensive care, maternity, nursing mothers, and children's wards on the first floor; and entrance, information, radiology, clinical medical service, outpatients, stretcher-patient delivery, emergency cases, administration, and cafeteria on the ground floor. The basement accommodates archive, physiotherapy, linear accelerator, radiation therapy, laboratory, and kitchen with service yard. The page gives approximate floor-height requirements and illustrates vertical and horizontal hospital sections.

Useful life
Structure, walls, fittings and finishings have different lifetimes.
The structure should if possible be framed in order to keep the
construction of the walls and partitions flexible. Medical equipment
is replaced after approx. 5-10 years according to department
and depreciation, which can have significant effect on the spatial
arrangements (e.g. linear accelerators, MRI scanners). The possible
installation and removal of such equipment without disrupting the
load-bearing structure should be taken into account in the design.

treatment area

Site
The site for a hospital needs enough space for the building, its
access and any possible extensions, and should be in a quiet
area. Contaminated ground should be avoided. Separated access
roads for visitors and patients, staff, goods and emergency
vehicles, as well as a helicopter pad, all need to be taken into
account in the selection of a site. The minimum land area for an
acute hospital with rectangular layout is approx. 15,000 m2 .
Orientation
The best orientation for treatment and operational rooms is
between north-west and north-east. For the fronts of patient
rooms, south-east or south-west is favourable, with pleasant
morning sun, little heat build-up, few sun protection measures
necessary and temperate evenings. East-west rooms in contrast
have deeper summer sun penetration but little winter sun.

Building forms
The form of the building is determined to a considerable extent
by the selection of access and routeing. A decision should be
reached at an early stage whether a design with a main corridor
(spine) and branches (transverse corridors) is chosen or whether
circulation will be radially outwards from a cruciform core.
Possible extensions and construction phases should be taken into
account. The vertical section of a hospital should be designed so
that the functions care, examination and treatment, supply and
waste disposal, delivery of patients on stretchers, service yard,
storage, administration and clinical medical service can be laid out
separately and reached quickly.
